TUNE-UP
Version 2.2 - November 1994
A Sandbox Software game, made with Game-Maker 3.0.

It's the morning of the Clown Club parade, and THE CHEZ won't run
right: Gwinn tipped the instrument trunk into the car. With no
wrenches, Doc Leo shrinks down and tunes it up by ear, with Sir
Reginald III, his rubber chicken, doing the fiddly bits.

To play, run TUNEUP.EXE (or PLAYGAME TUNEUP.GAM).
A Sound Blaster plays the music and the notes; the PC speaker plays
the notes without one.

Free to share: see LICENSE.TXT.

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
The Story

It is the morning of the Clown Club parade, and THE CHEZ is meant to lead it. Overnight, Gwinn buried Doc Leo's toolbox in the yard and tipped the Clown Club's instrument trunk in through the car's door window. Now THE CHEZ honks like a kazoo and rattles like a tambourine.

No wrenches? No problem. Doc Leo gives the car a tune-up by ear. He does his shrinking trick and climbs inside, and Sir Reginald III, his rubber chicken, does the fiddly bits: he fits where Doc Leo can't. Teddy rides along in the front passenger seat.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TUNEUP and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the notes; without one, the PC speaker plays the notes.

Pick Play from the menu. Before each level, Doc Leo taps his hat and pulls out the tool for the job, and a cutaway of THE CHEZ shows what is tuned so far. Then he and Sir Reginald III talk it over. Press a key to skip ahead.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Up hops; Q and E hop left and right. On a plug wire, Up climbs and Down climbs down. Space reaches up: hold it under a crank to turn it, or tap it to play a key. In Oil's Well, E G B D F squirt the oil can. In Pump Up the Volume, B twists a balloon dog that floats Doc Leo up. F2 shows what you have, F5 saves and F6 loads.

pages.head: Doc Leo and Sir Reginald III
pages.html:
Doc Leo and Sir Reginald III

Doc Leo is the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club: a chewed-up gray fedora with pins in its band, his own face paint, wire glasses, a patched navy corduroy jacket and red sneakers, and today a red shop rag in his pocket. He has an excellent ear.

Sir Reginald III is a rubber chicken of very good family. He does the repairs, tightens terminals with his beak and corrects Doc Leo's puns. Bump into him all you like; he is at work and does not mind.

A spark doesn't hurt Doc Leo; it frizzes his hair and costs a little energy. Energy comes back as you play: each note of the first key in The Timing Beat gives a little.

pages.head: The Dream Engine
pages.html:
The Dream Engine

1. Jump Start

The battery is flat. Find the red clamp on the shelf and the black clamp under the workbench: each opens its own terminal. Then stand under the crank and hold Space until the gauge is full.

2. Spark Plucks

The spark plugs are harp strings. Climb each wire and pluck its plug. Sparks run up the wires in the firing order, first, third, fourth, second: wait for yours to pass, then climb.

3. The Timing Beat

A paper roll turns across the top, and its holes drop notes down four glass tubes onto four keys. Stand under a key and tap Space as its note lands; right on the beat scores best. Three verses: a straight one, a syncopated one with a tube that splits in two and one that takes the long way round, and a quick one in double time. Each verse's gate opens when the meter at the top is full and you have played enough notes.

4. Oil's Well

Squeaks pace the five lines of a staff over Doc Leo's head. It's a treble clef staff, so each line is a note, and its letter is the key that squirts oil along it: E the bottom line, then G, B, D and F at the top. The letters sit at the lines' right ends. An oiled Squeak turns into a calm note that floats home to you. More Squeaks come out of the clef end as you go; bring every note home and the gate opens.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits and Registering

Tune-Up, version 2.0, November 1994. Design, art, music and programming by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic's AI model), made in code for Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition. Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs.

Starring Doc Leo as the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, Sir Reginald III as himself, Teddy and Gwinn. Doc Leo's poses follow the ones drawn for CERTIFIED RAT TICKLER. The songs are played on the music editor's instrument presets. No wrenches were harmed. Gwinn would like that on the record.

This is shareware

Copy it for your friends and upload it to your favorite BBS. If you enjoy it, please register for $15 with Sandbox Software, Dept. HONK-ZOO, P.O. Box 000 (a made-up address: please don't mail anything). Registered players get a cutaway poster of THE CHEZ, and our thanks.

news.head: Tune-Up: no wrenches, no problem
news.html: It's parade morning, THE CHEZ honks like a kazoo, and Gwinn has buried the toolbox. Our newest game, Tune-Up, sends Doc Leo inside the car to tune it up by ear, with Sir Reginald III, his rubber chicken, doing the fiddly bits. Crank the battery to a bugle call, pluck the spark plugs like a harp, play the timing back into step on four glass pipes and oil the Squeaks off a staff. A Sound Blaster is a very good idea.

news.head: Since last issue: Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure
news.html: The dog show is over, and Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure players are still not telling the BBS how the Best Behaved ring came out. Thank you. The most-asked question: can Gwinn really sit? Halfway, yes. Her tail has opinions.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Bouncy
news.html: The workshop smelled of vinegar for two days this month. Doc Leo read that a raw egg left in vinegar loses its shell and goes bouncy, and had to see it for himself. It worked. Sir Reginald III watched the whole time and called it "hardly the point of an egg." Teddy was not allowed to play with it. Gwinn was not asked.

news.head: In the workshop: One more Teddy
news.html: The Teddy trilogy ends next month with Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure: seventeen stops, every place and friend from the first two games, and a surprise Teddy knows nothing about. For the first time, you get to drive THE CHEZ. What is the occasion? We can't say. Gwinn made us promise.

news.head: Letters: "Does the tuba know it is a tuba?"
news.html: We asked. The tuba has not commented. It is, however, very good at keeping the beat, and it has never once knocked over a trunk. Write to us about the trunk.

items.title: Tune-Up Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. One answer at a time: Sir Reginald III is watching.

hints.a: Each door waits for something: a clamp, a pluck, enough notes, every oiled Squeak. Press F2 to see what you have, then keep going.
Press a key. Each cartoon is cut into short clips, so the next key gets you to the level.

hints.q: How do I get up to the shelf?
hints.a: Up the tire stacks, along the workbench, then a hop to the right (E) from the end of the bench.
Stand right under it and hold Space. Each reach turns it a notch; eight notches fill the gauge.
Stand beside the wire and watch. The sparks run first, third, fourth, second: when yours has just passed, step on and hold Up.
Watch the pipes, not the keys: the lowest note in a pipe lands next. Stand under its key and tap Space as it lights.
That's the Y-pipe. Either key counts. Stand between them and you might get both.

Each key is its line's note in the treble clef: E is the bottom line, then G, B, D, and F at the top (Every Good Boy Does Fine). The letters sit at the right end of the lines. Squirt a line when a Squeak is on it.
